children: ) shares are trading lower Wednesday afternoon as gold bullion prices decline under pressure from a strengthening U.S. dollar, rising Treasury yields and hawkish rate commentary from Federal Reserve leadership.
SPDR Gold Shares stock is trending lower.
The downturn across precious metals exchange-traded funds follows remarks delivered Tuesday by Richmond Federal Reserve Bank President
. Barkin said, “The risks to inflation outweigh the risks to maximum employment,” adding, “Last week’s rate hike will help restore price stability; we’ll see if more hikes are needed.”

Barkin said persistent inflationary pressures across consumer spending and manufacturing justify sustained policy tightening. His comments pushed Treasury yields higher and boosted the U.S. dollar, elevating the opportunity cost of holding nonyielding bullion.

Unlike bonds or cash equivalents, physical gold generates no interest, dividends or yield for its holders. As Treasury yields rise, investors forfeit increasingly higher guaranteed returns by keeping capital in bullion rather than income-generating assets.

Falling spot gold prices directly compress net asset values for physically backed commodities. With inflation measures continuing to run above central bank targets, expectations for elevated interest rates reduce the immediate attractiveness of non-interest-bearing physical reserves.

Additionally, the stronger dollar increases the purchase cost of dollar-denominated bullion for overseas buyers, dampening international commercial demand and driving temporary net capital outflows from physical gold trusts.
SPDR Gold Shares were down 1.71% at $393.21 at the time of publication on Wednesday,
